messages:
InfraBot: INCIDENT ALERT: GPU pool 'us-west-2-primary' hitting 98% GPU utilization; autoscaler failed to add nodes (reason: quota_exhausted). Observed queue growth on inference-router. https://metrics.internal/redwood/gpu/us-west-2-primary :alert:
Alex Kim: ack — I see the alert. starting to pull logs and recent deploys. paging oncall.
Priya Shah: I'm oncall — looking. Noticing a model rollout 10m ago (model:v3.4-canary) with modified max_context_tokens=16384; previous default was 8192. could that explain kv-cache jump?
Sean O'Connor: queue length spiking: inference-router queue ~1200 -> 3800 reqs (5m). 503s and throttles rising. Token generation per request averaged 2.5x prior.
Marta Lopez: autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts: 
```
2026-03-15T14:07:02Z autoscaler: request_scale +10 nodes
2026-03-15T14:07:12Z autoscaler: failed - provider_quota_exceeded (pool_limit=60)
2026-03-15T14:08:44Z autoscaler: request_scale +20 nodes
2026-03-15T14:08:55Z autoscaler: failed - insufficient_images_ready
```
Marta Lopez: looks like two problems: rollout increased per-request KV usage -> more GPUs needed; provider quotas + image warmup prevented quick scaling.
Priya Shah: impact estimate? which customers affected?
Alex Kim: preliminary alert fanout: ~18 customers on the affected pools; from SLO monitoring: 95p latency -> 3.2s (was 0.6s), error rate bumped 0.2% -> 3.8% across API keys hitting us-west-2-primary. Enterprise customers with pinned models saw tail latency.
PagerDuty: Handing off to Priya Shah (current oncall). @Priya Shah you have incoming page.
Priya Shah: Confirming takeover. Immediate mitigation proposals: 1) pause v3.4-canary rollout, 2) route traffic off us-west-2-primary to dedicated pools (if capacity), 3) temporary non-prod throttle and reduce max_concurrency for heavy routes. Which is fastest?
Sean O'Connor: fastest is traffic routing change. We can patch routing table to divert 60% of traffic to us-west-2-burst (has spare capacity) and 40% to reserved-dedicated pools. But need to ensure model variant compatibility. v3.4-canary supports a compatible lighter variant: v3.4-compact (uses smaller KV encoding).
Marta Lopez: I can apply the routing override now. running: 
```
engops@console> rdctl routing set --from-pool us-west-2-primary --split 60:us-west-2-burst,40:reserved-dedicated --match model:v3.4
apply: ok
```
Marta Lopez: route change applied. monitor: queue length falling from 3800 -> 2200 in 90s. GPU util -> 88%.
Priya Shah: also pausing canary rollout in control plane (canary manager). Priya runs: 
```
pm-api: POST /canary/v3.4/pause
response: 200 ok
```
Alex Kim: pausing confirmed. No new v3.4 instances launched.
Sean O'Connor: still seeing heavy kv-cache per active session. can we force older model variant (v3.3) for keys with high traffic?
Marta Lopez: yes doing a targeted rollback for the canary cohort: routing rule to map api_key:heavy-customers -> model:v3.3. 
```
engops@console> rdctl routing patch --selector "api_key in (acct-123, acct-789)" --set model=v3.3
```
Marta Lopez: patch applied. Affected accounts are routed to v3.3. queue for those accounts dropping.
Priya Shah: Customer impact note: we should notify customers in the incident header: brief: degraded latency & intermittent throttling in us-west-2 for requests to model v3.4 variant. mitigation: traffic diversion and rollback for pinned customers. ETA for stability 15-25m.
Alex Kim: adding metrics snapshot: 
- peak queue length: 3850 (14:09:12)
- peak GPU util: 98% (14:10:05)
- max scale attempts: 3 over 6m
- error rate (5m): 3.8% -> primarily 503 and timeout
Priya Shah: ok next: can we drain the queue and avoid hard rollback? prefer safe rollback for prod customers pinned to v3.4. If queue drains in 20m then we can re-evaluate.
Marta Lopez: queue drain rate now ~120 reqs/s. based on that estimate drain ~18m to safe levels. GPU util down to 72% after routing override.
EngOps: FYI we have a pending cloud quota increase request but approval takes 2-4 hours. Not viable for immediate mitigation.
Sean O'Connor: recommend also adding temporary per-route token_limit to reduce per-request kv-cache usage: set max_context_tokens=8192 for non-enterprise routes.
Priya Shah: applying token_limit override for public routes now. 
```
control> rdctl model-config update --model v3.4 --set max_context_tokens=8192 --scope public_routes
applied: 200
```
Priya Shah: override live. expecting less KV memory per session.
Alex Kim: monitoring shows per-session KV bytes down ~45% for public routes within 2m. nice.
PagerDuty: Update: escalation to oncall team acknowledged; no escalation to execs yet.
Marta Lopez: Autoscaler is still limited by image warmup for new nodes. long-term: pre-pull images to warm pool. adding task in follow-ups.
Priya Shah: Current status at 14:22Z: queue 980, GPU util 44%, error rate 0.6%. Rolling status: canary paused, targeted rollbacks done, routing overrides in place, token limits applied. Begin incident containment -> degrade->recover timeline.
Alex Kim: customers notified via support banner and targeted emails for pinned enterprise customers.
Priya Shah: Assigning postmortem owners: Alex Kim (incident lead), Marta Lopez (infra root cause), Sean O'Connor (routing & throttling), EngOps (quota/limits). Creating ticket: RW-INC-2026-2142.
Priya Shah: immediate P0 mitigations done. Next steps: detailed root cause: why v3.4 changed default context without perf gating; autoscaler/gcp quota interplay; image warmup. Postmortem doc link will be posted here when ready.
Alex Kim: thanks everyone — keep monitoring for 30m then we close. :thumbsup:
Marta Lopez: adding follow-up to backlog: pre-pull model images on nodes, autoscaler improvement for graceful backoff and warm pool, prompt-level context caps, rollout gating by observed kv-memory.
EngOps: Noted. will file cloud quota expedite request and outreach to provider.
Priya Shah: closing notes: Incident contained at 14:25Z, full recovery confirmed at 14:30Z. Will update channel when the postmortem is up. :white_check_mark:
